# Operational Workflow

## Do not Modify Auto-generated Files

**Never edit** `Types.lean`, `/Funs.lean` or `translation.json` — these
are auto-generated by Aeneas.

**Never edit** the Rust sources (`src/`, `build.rs`, `Cargo.toml` apart from its
`[package.metadata.charon]` section), they are kept identical
to the pinned upstream commit.

If the translation fails or produces unusable output, fix it with a translation patch in
`translation-patches/` (one function per patch, applied only while extracting), or by marking the item `exclude`/`opaque`
(in `[package.metadata.charon]` in `Cargo.toml`), then re-extract.

To learn more about Aeneas and how it extracts Rust into Lean, see the [Aeneas documentation](https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas/tree/main/documentation).

## Updating the Import File after Adding, Removing, or Renaming `.lean` Files

After adding, removing, or renaming any `.lean` file, run:

```bash
lake exe mk_all --git
```

to regenerate the root import files that list every module in the project.

## Linting

To lint the Lean code, use `lake exe runLinter Spqr`.

## PR Workflow and Formatting

All PRs, unless special circumstances are justified, must close an open issue in the project.

Whenever possible, a PR should address exactly one issue, and its scope should be as small as possible to achieve that goal, ideally not exceeding ~500LOC (except for refactoring and documentation-focused PRs).

If two or more issues are closed by a PR, they need to be related in some sensible way, otherwise the PR should be closed and reopened as two or more smaller PRs with tighter focus.

In general it is best to open an issue or discuss with the others working on the project before starting work on a PR in order to avoid duplication of work.

PRs are reviewed when marked as ready (i.e., not a draft) and all checks have passed.
After the PR is created (or marked as ready) the author should hold off on meaningful changes until after the review process, to avoid reviewers looking at outdated code.
After review the author is solely responsible for merging in the accepted PR, and is expected to do so in a timely manner.

The expected format for PR title, body, and footer is:

**Title format:** PRs closing verification issues should mimic the issue titles being closed (i.e. "Verify/Prove/Specify `foo` in `bar.rs`"). Other PR titles should use imperative present tense ("add" not "added") and no trailing period.

**Body format:** The first paragraph must start with "This PR". Use imperative present tense. Include motivation and contrast with previous behaviour where relevant. Do NOT use markdown headings (## Summary, ## Test plan, etc.) in PR bodies. If relevant, include the full name of the function(s) which the PR concerns so that the PR can be found by various automation.

**Footer format:** A footer is mandatory and must contain the following:
- Breaking changes (if any): All breaking changes have to be mentioned in footer with the description of the change, justification and migration notes
- Referencing issues: Closed issues should be listed on a separate line in the footer prefixed with "Closes" keyword, e.g., `Closes #123, #456`.

**Lables:** PRs are encouraged, but not required, to use the same labels as the underlying issues they close, especially if they are not verification-related.

## Proof cheats

- Some statements are externally verified and we do not replicate their proofs, for various reasons. In such instances, we use the `axiom` keyword. The documentation associated with each instance of `axiom` must list the source of its external verification.
- We do not use of the `externally_verified` tag in this repository. Use `axiom` instead.
- Functions that are not translated (external crates, items marked `opaque` in
  `aeneas-config.yml`) are declared in `SrcTranslated/FunsExternal.lean` as `noncomputable opaque`
  signatures, never as `axiom`: a signature carries no assumption. Their behaviour is stated
  separately as property axioms, preferably in WP form with `@[step]` (e.g.
  `spqr.kdf.hkdf_to_slice_spec`), so that every trusted assumption about them is a named axiom.
- Our CI flags any PR that introduces new `sorry` statements. In such an event, the following is expected, based on the nature of the property proven via `sorry`:
	- if the `sorry` serves as a placeholder for a proof that intends to be completed later, the PR author should open a new issue documenting this placeholder and link the issue number in a TODO comment next to the `sorry`.
	- if the `sorry` substitutes the proof of an externally verified property, to be treated as an axiom, the author should use the `axiom` keyword instead.

## Performance

All PRs are expected to consider the performance impact they may have on verification time/CI.

Upon opening a PR, you may call `!radar`, to invoke our performance analysis tool.

See our [performance tracking guidelines](./PERFORMANCE.md) for more information.

## AI contributions

### Quick Codex review

A collaborator with repository write access can post exactly `!review` as a new
comment in an open PR's conversation (including fork PRs). Edits to comments and
inline review comments do not trigger it. The bot posts a new comment with a quick
static review using [the AI review questions](AI_PR_REVIEW_QUESTIONS.md) and the
reviewer, style, and workflow guides from the trusted default-branch revision.
It reports findings by severity and category, with evidence and precise locations.
It does not approve PRs or generate specifications.

The bot reads the pinned diff, relevant source through Git, PR metadata, existing
comments (including performance and sorry-delta reports), and head CI checks. It
does not run builds, lint, trust audits, extraction, or benchmarks. Its comment
identifies these limits and the reviewed commits. Full validation and human review
remain necessary. If either the head or base changes while it works, its comment
is marked outdated; post a new `!review` to review the updated PR. Failed runs post
a link to the workflow logs. Each review job has a 15-minute timeout.

To enable the bot, merge `.github/workflows/codex-review.yml`, its prompt, and
`scripts/codex-review.cjs` into the default branch, enable GitHub Actions, and add
an Actions secret named `OPENAI_API_KEY` with API access and billing. Optionally
set the Actions variable `CODEX_REVIEW_MODEL`; otherwise the Codex action chooses
its default model. API usage is billed to that key. Repository/organization policy
must permit the workflow's read permissions and the publishing job's
`pull-requests: write` permission. No separate GitHub PAT or bot account is needed.

The workflow checks the requester's current write permission before using the key.
It never checks out or runs PR code: Codex uses a read-only sandbox with sudo
removed, and only the separate publishing job can write comments. PR content is
untrusted review evidence; it cannot replace the trusted prompt or guides.
Implementation uses the [official Codex GitHub Action](https://developers.openai.com/codex/github-action).
Run the bot's offline checks with `node --test scripts/codex-review.test.cjs`.

### Contribution policy

**Specifications:** PRs introducing AI-generated specifications of any kind are strictly prohibited, and their submission may result in a contribution ban at the maintainers' discretion.

**Proofs:** AI-generated proofs are welcome, as long as they are compliant with the style guide and requirements listed in this document. The human submitting the PR is held responsible for the contents of the PR, in particular its adherence to style and contribution guidelines, as well as the performance impact outlined above.
